summary: Under NSW Crimes Act 1900 s.86 (detain for advantage/kidnapping, basic max 14 years; 25 years if in company or with wounding/GBH), the cited R v Kerr involved detention under threat of violence for around 36 hours.
label_raw: Australia (NSW) — Crimes Act 1900 s.86 statutory anchor + R v Kerr
source_citation: NSW Crimes Act 1900 s.86 (basic s.86(1) max 14 yrs; 25 yrs if in company per s.86(2)/86A or with wounding/GBH); R v Kerr cited in NSW Judicial Commission Sentencing Bench Book (victim detained under threat of violence around 36 hours). https://www.judcom.nsw.gov.au/publications/benchbks/sentencing/kidnapping.html — penalty_jail_years recorded as basic statutory max (14 yrs).

summary: In R v Mills (1998, BC CA) a kidnapping in which the victim was driven around for several hours drew sentences of roughly 4 to 5 years, showing that even brief detentions attract multi-year custody.
label_raw: Canada — R v Mills, 1998 CanLII 15020 (BC CA)
source_citation: R v Mills, 1998 CanLII 15020 (BC CA); 4-5 yrs (co-accused Babin 4 yrs; Mills ~5 yrs) for kidnapping, victim driven around several hours. Criminal Law Notebook, https://criminalnotebook.ca/index.php/Kidnapping_and_Unlawful_Confinement_(Sentencing_Cases) — short detention drawing multi-year sentence (sub-linear scaling reference).

summary: Canada's Criminal Code s.279(2) forcible/unlawful confinement carries a maximum of 10 years on indictment (18 months summary) with no stated minimum detention period, providing a federal statutory liberty-deprivation anchor.
label_raw: Canada — Criminal Code s.279(2) forcible/unlawful confinement statutory anchor
source_citation: Criminal Code (Canada) s.279(2) (max 10 yrs on indictment / max 18 mo summary); s.279(1) kidnapping with aggravating factors mandatory minimum 5 yrs (7 with priors), max life. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/c-46/section-279.html — no stated minimum period.

summary: Germany's StGB §239(1) basic offence punishes unlawful confinement of any short duration (hours to days, below the 1-week threshold) with up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine, serving as the sub-week lower-bound anchor.
source_citation: Strafgesetzbuch (StGB) §239(1) (up to 5 years or fine, no duration floor); https://dejure.org/gesetze/StGB/239.html — lower-bound anchor distinguishing sub-week from over-week confinement.

summary: Germany's StGB §239(3) raises the punishment range to 1-10 years when unlawful deprivation of liberty exceeds exactly one week, giving an explicit legislative step function for detention duration.
label_raw: Germany — §239(3) StGB statutory threshold (deprivation of liberty > 1 week)
source_citation: Strafgesetzbuch (StGB) §239(3), text "länger als eine Woche"; https://dejure.org/gesetze/StGB/239.html and official English at https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/englisch_stgb/englisch_stgb.html (aggravated range 1-10 yrs triggered by confinement exceeding one week; §239(4) not under 3 yrs if victim dies).

summary: The England & Wales Sentencing Council kidnap/false imprisonment guideline treats a prolonged captivity period as a High culpability factor (range up to 16 years, statutory max life), with a 2022 immediate-custody average of 5 years 9 months.
harm_duration: prolonged period (High culpability factor; duration is a culpability multiplier, not a fixed per-time rate)
label_raw: UK (England & Wales) — Kidnap/False Imprisonment Sentencing Guideline (Sentencing Council)
source_citation: Sentencing Council Kidnap/False Imprisonment guideline (offence range community order up to 16 yrs; statutory max life; "victim held captive over a prolonged period" is a High culpability factor; 2022 immediate-custody average custodial sentence length 5 yrs 9 mo post guilty-plea). https://sentencingcouncil.org.uk/guidelines/kidnap-false-imprisonment/ — duration is a culpability multiplier rather than a fixed per-time rate.

summary: In a Sheffield Crown Court trafficking/false imprisonment case (2023) two men chained to radiators and starved for just under two weeks led to sentences of nearly 20 years each, reflecting a high penalty-per-time due to torture-like aggravation.
label_raw: UK (England & Wales) — Sheffield Crown Court trafficking/false imprisonment case (two defendants)
source_citation: Sheffield Crown Court trafficking/false imprisonment case, 2023; nearly 20 years each (two Albanian men chained to radiators, starved). https://www.thestar.co.uk/news/crime/sheffield-crown-court-men-jailed-for-nearly-20-years-following-deeply-disturbing-false-imprisonment-case-3973189 — high penalty-per-time because aggravated by torture-like conditions (forced labour, violence, starvation); must be isolated from pure liberty_time.

summary: In R v Amanda Wixon (Gloucestershire Crown Court, 2026) the victim was held captive for over 20 years (since 1996, discovered March 2021) yet the false-imprisonment-plus-forced-labour sentence was 13 years, illustrating strongly sub-linear scaling.
label_raw: UK (England & Wales) — R v Amanda Wixon, Gloucestershire Crown Court
source_citation: R v Amanda Wixon, Gloucestershire Crown Court, sentenced 2026; 13 years (1 count false imprisonment + 2 counts forced/compulsory labour + 3 counts assault); victim held captive since 1996, discovered March 2021. CPS https://www.cps.gov.uk/south-west/news/gloucestershire-woman-who-imprisoned-victim-over-20-years-jailed — illustrates strong sub-linear scaling (20+ yrs deprivation -> 13 yrs custody).

summary: California Penal Code §§236/237 punishes felony false imprisonment by violence, menace, fraud, or deceit on a 16-month/2-year/3-year triad with no minimum detention period, providing a statutory liberty-deprivation anchor.
harm_duration: any (statute states no minimum period; restraint can be brief)
label_raw: USA (California) — Penal Code §§236/237 statutory anchor (felony false imprisonment by violence/menace/fraud/deceit)
source_citation: California Penal Code §§236-237 (felony triad 16 mo / 2 yr / 3 yr; misdemeanor up to 1 yr county jail; elderly/dependent-adult victim up to 4 yr, 5 if injury). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PEN&sectionNum=236 — statute states no minimum period (restraint can be brief).

summary: In United States v. Brian David Mitchell (D. Utah, 2011), the kidnapping and sexual assault of 14-year-old Elizabeth Smart over ~9 months (June 2002-March 2003) drew two consecutive life sentences without parole.
label_raw: USA (federal) — United States v. Brian David Mitchell (Elizabeth Smart kidnapping)
source_citation: United States v. Brian David Mitchell, D. Utah, sentenced 2011; two life sentences no parole (abducted 5 Jun 2002, recovered ~12 Mar 2003; kidnapping + sexual assault of a minor). FBI press release https://archives.fbi.gov/archives/saltlakecity/press-releases/2011/slc052511a.htm ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidnapping_of_Elizabeth_Smart (penalty blended with sexual assault; life sentence = saturation, jail-years not numerically expressible).

summary: In State v. Ariel Castro (Ohio, 2013) the captivity of three women for roughly 9-11 years each, compounded with rape and aggravated murder of a fetus, drew life without parole plus 1,000 years and a $100,000 fine.
label_raw: USA (Ohio) — State v. Ariel Castro (Cleveland kidnappings)
source_citation: State v. Ariel Castro, Ohio, sentenced 2013; life without parole + 1,000 years + $100,000 fine (~$135k in 2024 USD); pleaded to 937 counts incl. kidnapping, rape, aggravated murder of a fetus. Victims: Michelle Knight ~11 yrs (from Aug 2002), Amanda Berry ~10 yrs (Apr 2003), Gina DeJesus ~9 yrs (Apr 2004), all rescued 6 May 2013. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariel_Castro_kidnappings — extreme outlier; multi-year confinement compounded with rape/murder; upper-bound saturation point, not a clean per-time ratio.

summary: In State v. William Mozingo Jr. (Summit County, Ohio, 2024) the defendant held victim Chloe Jones hostage in a garage for 4 days and received an indefinite 25 to 31.5 year sentence, aggravated by violence/assault.
label_raw: USA (Ohio) — State v. William Mozingo Jr., Summit County (Akron)
source_citation: State v. William Mozingo Jr., Summit County (Akron), Ohio, sentenced 2024; indefinite 25-31.5 yr sentence (deliberate abduction + assault with baseball bat). https://myfox28columbus.com/amp/news/nation-world/william-mozingo-junior-serial-kidnapper-held-ohio-woman-hostage-beat-her-baseball-bat-learns-his-fate-conviction-cincinnati-kidnapping-high-profile-court-cases-verdict-summit-county-assault (penalty blended with violence/assault).
